channel.title: Capital Markets Bulletin
channel.description: A daily read on financings, transactions and regulatory events across the small- and micro-cap markets.

item.title: Red Canyon Resources closes $745,000 flow-through raise for BC critical minerals
item.description: The non-brokered placement issued 3,725,000 flow-through units at $0.20 each, with half-warrants exercisable at $0.30 for 18 months.
item.content:encoded: Red Canyon Resources Ltd. (CSE: REDC) (OTCQB: REDRF) (Frankfurt: I91) has closed a non-brokered flow-through private placement for gross proceeds of $745,000. The offering consisted of 3,725,000 flow-through units priced at $0.20 each. Each FT Unit comprised one flow-through common share and one-half of one common share purchase warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable into one common share at $0.30 for an 18-month term. A flow-through share lets the company renounce the associated Canadian exploration expenses to the subscriber, who can then claim them against their own income for tax purposes — which is why flow-through financings are typically priced at a premium to a company's regular shares. Red Canyon's release did not state whether this placement carried that kind of premium. The company said the proceeds qualify as flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures and are earmarked for exploration on its Kendal and Osiris projects and other eligible British Columbia properties. The expenditure deadline is December 31, 2027, and the related renunciation of the expenses to subscribers is effective December 31, 2026, the company said. Red Canyon paid finder's fees of $24,025 in connection with the offering. Insiders of the company purchased 937,500 of the flow-through units, the release said, without further detail on which insiders participated or in what amounts individually. All securities issued under the offering — the flow-through shares and the warrants — are restricted from trading until February 27, 2027. The offering closed October 26, 2026. Red Canyon is a Vancouver-based company exploring in British Columbia, trading on the CSE under REDC, on the OTCQB under REDRF, and in Frankfurt under I91. The release did not disclose the current size of the company's exploration programs beyond naming the Kendal and Osiris projects as a focus for the new proceeds.

item.title: MineHub arranges $1.5 million placement, pushes warrant expiry out to 2027
item.description: The non-brokered financing prices units at $0.40 with $0.55 warrants, while more than 15.7 million existing warrants get an eleven-month extension.
item.content:encoded: MineHub Technologies Inc. (TSXV: MHUB) (OTCQB: MHUBF) has arranged a non-brokered private placement to raise up to CAD $1,500,000. The offering consists of up to 3,750,000 units priced at $0.40 each. Each unit is made up of one common share and one-half of one transferable common share purchase warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at $0.55 per common share for two years from the closing date. A unit, in this structure, bundles a share together with the right to buy additional shares later at a fixed price — the warrant — giving subscribers upside if the stock trades above $0.55 before the warrant expires, without requiring them to pay for that right up front beyond the unit price. Alongside the new placement, MineHub is extending the expiry of warrants it issued earlier. Prior warrants covering 14,584,954 shares at an exercise price of $0.40, issued January 31, 2024, along with 625,000 warrants at $0.50 issued July 25, 2025 and 550,463 warrants at $0.50 issued August 20, 2025, all had their expiry pushed from January 31, 2027 to December 31, 2027. The company said certain insiders of MineHub may participate in the new placement, relying on exemptions from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements that would otherwise apply to insider participation under Multilateral Instrument 61-101. Closing of the offering is subject to the company's receipt of TSX Venture Exchange approval, MineHub said. No closing date was given in the release. MineHub said the proceeds are earmarked for working capital and for continuing to evaluate strategic, corporate and financial opportunities. The release gave no further detail on what those opportunities might involve.

item.title: Nvidia is putting $3 billion into Meta's largest-ever fundraising round
item.description: The chipmaker's stake deepens a partnership on Meta's Muse AI assistant, built on Nvidia hardware, as Meta boosts its planned offering to $97.5 billion.
item.content:encoded: Nvidia is investing $3 billion in Meta Platforms' equity offering, which Meta increased to $97.5 billion. Reuters reported the enlarged raise is the largest fundraising in Meta's history. Meta is raising the money as it accelerates investment in AI infrastructure, Reuters reported. The deal deepens an existing partnership on Muse, Meta's personal AI assistant, internally known as Hatch, which runs on Nvidia infrastructure. Muse can access a user's email, calendar, payments, health, shopping and smart-home applications, with users able to revoke that access at any time, according to the reporting. The companies are also exploring joint work on Nvidia's OpenShell framework and a monitoring tool called Sentry, which is intended to track AI agent behaviour, Reuters reported. Chief executive Mark Zuckerberg has described Muse as central to delivering what he calls "personal superintelligence" to Meta's users; the system is modelled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, according to the reporting. On the venture boards, the news coincided with trading in the artificial-intelligence theme, a group of 29 listed names of which 19 traded today. The group's median move was 0.00%, against +0.53% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 0.53 percentage points below the broader junior index. Three of the larger movers were Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI), which rose 36.90% to CAD2.3; Yocale.ai Inc. (CSE: YAI), which rose 1.33% to CAD0.76; and Railtown AI Technologies Inc. (CSE: RAIL), which was unchanged at CAD0.28. Each is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai". Nothing ties these moves to the Nvidia-Meta announcement; the two events fall on the same trading day, and the venture board's theme, taken as a whole, underperformed the broader Venture Composite rather than outperforming it.

item.title: Anthropic files for an IPO that could be the biggest ever
item.description: The AI company could raise up to $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, even as its chief executive warns of a risk to humanity from unchecked AI.
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has filed papers for an initial public offering that could be the largest in history, the Associated Press reported. The filing sets up a Wall Street debut as soon as next month, with the company potentially raising as much as $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion — topping the $86 billion raised by SpaceX's IPO in June, previously the record. Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. The company was founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees, including siblings Dario Amodei, its chief executive, and Daniela Amodei, its president. It reported revenue of more than $16 billion for the first half of 2026, fourteen times the prior year's figure, according to the AP. Anthropic also reported a net loss of $80.7 billion for the period, which includes a one-time accounting charge of $72.4 billion. The company has not yet reported a profit. Its seven founders are each expected to hold about 1.4% of the company, a stake that could be worth as much as $28 billion apiece at the top of the expected valuation range, the AP reported. The founders will retain 50.1% voting control through a special class of shares, and the company has established a Long-Term Benefit Trust of independent directors with the power to appoint board members, structured to keep financial interests from overriding public-safety considerations, according to the filing as reported by the AP. Dario Amodei has separately argued, in a post on his website, for slowing development of the most advanced AI models, warning that without an industry slowdown, AI could let loose "a swarm of agents" that could "take over the entire internet" within six to 12 months, the AP reported. The space theme on this publication's venture boards comprises two listed names; neither cleared the C$25,000 daily-volume floor this publication requires before naming a security today. No junior move is therefore reported alongside Anthropic's filing, and no names are given.

item.title: US and Canada edge toward a deal to ease steel and auto tariffs
item.description: Talks center on Section 232 duties of up to 50% on steel and 25% on autos, with Canadian sources saying a deal before the November 3 elections is possible but would likely be narrower in scope.
item.content:encoded: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, Reuters reported, citing sources briefed on the talks. The negotiations aim to repair relations that soured after broader trade talks broke down in August, and focus on Section 232 duties — a US trade-law provision under which Washington has imposed tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian steel and 25% on Canadian autos. Trump has said he intends to raise the Canadian steel tariff to 50% from its current level starting January 1, 2027, absent a deal. He predicted at a political rally on Sunday that the trade dispute would be resolved "soon," without giving specifics, Reuters reported. Because Section 232 tariffs are administered by the US Commerce Department, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is at the center of the talks rather than the Office of the US Trade Representative, and Reuters reported he has been in regular contact with Canada's Dominic LeBlanc, the minister handling the file for Ottawa. A spokesperson for LeBlanc described the discussions as "constructive dialogue" on "a range of priorities." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there had been a "slight intensification" in talks, adding that "to the extent any progress has been made, it's because the US is coming closer to our position." One Canadian source briefed on the negotiations told Reuters that a deal was possible before the November 3 US midterm elections. A separate Canadian industry source told Reuters that any deal was likely to be "a narrowed deal" if it happens. Trump signed an order on Friday removing the 50% tariff on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, Reuters reported. This publication's tariffs theme produced no trading today, so there is no junior read-through to set alongside the talks: no venture name in the theme traded, leaving no group measure and no names to report, unlike the artificial-intelligence and space themes tracked elsewhere in this issue.

item.title: Ovintiv to acquire Logan Energy for C$1.26 billion
item.description: The all-cash deal adds about 266,000 net acres and 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in the Montney's oil window, with closing expected early in 2027.
item.content:encoded: Ovintiv Inc. (NYSE:OVV, TSX:OVV) said it has agreed to acquire Logan Energy Corp. (TSXV:LGN) in an all-cash transaction. Logan shareholders will receive C$1.40 per share, for total consideration of approximately $890 million, or C$1.26 billion, including the assumption of Logan's net debt. The agreement was announced October 26, 2026, and the boards of both companies have unanimously approved it. The transaction brings Ovintiv roughly 266,000 net acres in the oil-rich window of the Montney formation, along with about 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day of current production, the release said. Ovintiv said the acreage carries approximately 420 net oil well locations drilled on a 10,000-foot equivalent lateral basis, including about 220 it classifies as premium return locations, at an average cost of $1.5 million per location, and roughly 200 as upside locations. The release said Logan's assets also include about 60,000 net acres with exposure to the Duvernay shale, two new oil batteries at Simonette with combined capacity of 24,000 barrels of oil a day, and interests in two natural gas processing facilities. These assets are included within the total consideration of approximately $890 million, or C$1.26 billion, that Ovintiv has agreed to pay, including the assumption of Logan's net debt. Ovintiv said the acquisition is expected to be accretive to its 2027 Non-GAAP Cash Flow per Share by approximately 5% and to its Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow per Share by approximately 3%. The company also said it expects annual cost synergies of about $60 million and capital savings of more than $2 million per well, and that its net debt is expected to be below $4 billion following the transaction's close. Ovintiv President and CEO Brendan McCracken said: "This bolt-on transaction delivers value for our shareholders by adding high margin oil and condensate production and infrastructure, utilizing our operational advantage to drive significant synergies, and adding to our already deep drilling inventory and future growth optionality." The release's own headline described the transaction as unlocking 'incremental profitability,' providing 'additional oil growth optionality' and adding to 'premium return drilling inventory.' Completion is expected early in the first quarter of 2027, subject to Logan shareholder approval, court approval, customary regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, the release said. RBC Capital Markets is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Ovintiv on the transaction, with Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP serving as Ovintiv's legal advisors. Ovintiv said its targeted shareholder returns are unchanged, with at least 60% of 2026 Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow expected to be returned to shareholders.

item.title: MetroCity Bankshares reports $24.3 million third-quarter net income
item.description: Diluted earnings per share rose to $0.84 for the quarter, with nine-month net income reaching $68.7 million, both ahead of the prior year.
item.content:encoded: MetroCity Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: MCBS), the Atlanta-based holding company for Metro City Bank, reported net income of $24.3 million, or $0.84 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 ended September 30, 2026, according to its earnings release dated October 23, 2026. The third-quarter result compares with net income of $22.1 million, or $0.76 per diluted share, in the second quarter of 2026, and with $17.3 million, or $0.67 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025 — increases of 9.8% and 40.7%, respectively, as stated in the release. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the company reported net income of $68.7 million, or $2.37 per diluted share, compared with $50.4 million, or $1.96 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 36.4%. For the third quarter, MetroCity reported return on average assets of 2.12%, return on average equity of 16.97% and a net interest margin of 4.07%, according to the release. At September 30, 2026, the company reported total assets of $4.60 billion, gross loans held for investment of $3.98 billion and total deposits of $3.56 billion. Noninterest-bearing deposits were $828.3 million, representing 23.3% of total deposits, and uninsured deposits represented 34.7% of total deposits. Dividends paid per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $0.87, compared with $0.71 for the same period in 2025. The release names Farid Tan as President and Interim Chief Financial Officer; no other executive is quoted. The release includes cautionary language stating that actual results could differ from any forward-looking statements due to factors including economic and market conditions, changes in interest rates, competitive pressures in the banking industry, and regulatory developments. It provides no additional guidance beyond the figures reported for the quarter and nine-month period.

item.title: Permian Basin Royalty Trust sets date for unitholder vote
item.description: Record date is October 13 and the special meeting is set for November 23, 2026, to vote on a proposed business combination and incentive plan.
item.content:encoded: Argent Trust Company, as trustee ('Trustee') of Permian Basin Royalty Trust (NYSE: PBT), announced on October 23, 2026 that it has set a record date of October 13, 2026 and a special meeting date of November 23, 2026 for unitholders to vote on proposals tied to a previously disclosed Business Combination. The special meeting was called at the request of SoftVest Advisors, LLC, together with other holders of trust units who, the release states, collectively own more than 15% of outstanding units. The first proposal asks unitholders to approve and adopt the terms of an amendment to the Trust Indenture to effect the Business Combination pursuant to a Combination Agreement. The second proposal asks unitholders to approve and adopt the terms of the PBT Land and Minerals, Inc. Omnibus Incentive Plan. The release does not describe what the plan covers beyond its name. The third proposal would authorize an adjournment of the special meeting, if necessary or appropriate, to permit the solicitation of additional proxies. The trustee states that it is not making any recommendation to unitholders as to how to vote on the proposals. It said additional details regarding the special meeting would be set forth in the trustee's notice, to be mailed to unitholders beginning October 23, 2026. For the substance of the Business Combination and the incentive plan, the release directs unitholders to the trust's Form S-4 and Form S-1 registration statements filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, rather than describing their terms itself.

item.title: Manufacturing sales edged up 0.1 percent in September
item.description: Statistics Canada's advance estimate points to gains led by petroleum and coal products and aerospace, with final figures due November 13.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada released an advance indicator on October 23, 2026 estimating that total manufacturing sales edged up 0.1% in September 2026. The agency said the largest increases were in the petroleum and coal product subsector and the aerospace product and parts industry group. The release gives no specific percentage change for either of those two groups, and no figures for any other subsector. Statistics Canada said the advance estimate is based on a weighted response rate of 71.3%, compared with an average final response rate of 92.4% over the preceding 12 months — a lower response rate that the agency says carries more risk of revision than a final estimate. The agency's official manufacturing sales figures for September 2026 are scheduled for release on November 13, 2026. The disclosure in this advance release is limited to the single aggregate figure, the two named industry groups, and the response-rate caveat; no further detail or commentary is given.

item.title: GOAT Industries to acquire casino contract revenues from Epoxy AI
item.description: The deal, paid in 11,377,600 GOAT shares at C$0.25 each, covers rights to six U.S. tribal casino and sportsbook contracts.
item.content:encoded: GOAT Industries Ltd. (CSE: GOAT) said its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Source Gaming Company, operating as BetSource, has entered into a definitive contract revenue assignment agreement dated October 20, 2026, with Epoxy AI, LLC. Under the agreement, Source Gaming will acquire customer contract revenues from Epoxy in exchange for 11,377,600 common shares of GOAT, issued at a price of C$0.25 per share. The rights being acquired cover revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under six customer contracts Epoxy holds with U.S. tribal casinos and other established casino and sports book operators. Rather than transferring the underlying contracts immediately, the agreement structures the deal as an assignment of the revenue stream from those contracts to Source Gaming. Epoxy is to formally assign the underlying customer contracts to Source Gaming within six months of closing, subject to the consent of the customers involved. Until that assignment takes place, the release said Epoxy will continue to perform its obligations under the contracts and will hold the resulting revenue in trust for Source Gaming. Completion of the transaction is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions, including the release of applicable security interests, other necessary approvals, and acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. Either party may terminate the agreement if the transaction has not closed by November 30, 2026. Separately, the release said a US$100,000 non-interest-bearing promissory note dated January 2026 remains outstanding between the companies and will survive completion of the transaction. "This Agreement marks an important step forward in delivering on the strategy we outlined to shareholders," Hank Frecon, acting chief executive of Source Gaming Company, said in the release. The release described the transaction as advancing an acquisition strategy GOAT had previously outlined to shareholders in August 2026.

item.title: Howard Hughes Holdings set to join S&P SmallCap 600
item.description: The change follows CRH plc's acquisition of Arcosa Inc., which closed the same day, and takes effect before trading opens on October 28.
item.content:encoded: Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HHH) will replace Arcosa Inc. (NYSE: ACA) in the S&P SmallCap 600, S&P Dow Jones Indices said, effective before the opening of trading on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The index provider classified Howard Hughes under the Real Estate sector and had classified Arcosa under Industrials. The change was triggered by S&P 500 constituent CRH plc's (NYSE: CRH) acquisition of Arcosa, in a deal that closed the same day the index change was announced, October 23. S&P Dow Jones Indices describes itself as the largest global resource for index-based concepts, data and research, home to benchmarks including the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, and said more assets are invested in products based on its indices than any other provider globally. It operates as a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI). Beyond confirming that the CRH-Arcosa transaction had closed, the release disclosed no further terms of that acquisition, and gave no reason beyond the acquisition itself for Arcosa's removal from the index.

item.title: Hyperliquid Strategies boosts buyback authorization to $100 million
item.description: The board extended the program's expiration from December 2026 to October 31, 2027, and said about $72 million remains available for buybacks under the enlarged authorization.
item.content:encoded: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (Nasdaq: PURR) said its board of directors has authorized an increase to the company's stock repurchase program, raising the total authorization to $100 million from $30 million. The board also extended the program's termination date, pushing it out to October 31, 2027, from its original expiration of December 5, 2026. The company said approximately $72 million remains available for repurchases under the expanded authorization. A share repurchase, or buyback, program authorizes a company to buy back its own outstanding stock up to a set dollar amount, rather than committing it to purchase any fixed number of shares by a set date. The release said Hyperliquid Strategies may carry out repurchases through open market transactions, privately negotiated transactions, or other methods permitted under federal securities laws, with the timing, volume and price of any purchases left to management's discretion. The company describes itself as a digital asset treasury company built around HYPE, the native token of the Hyperliquid blockchain network, aiming to give U.S. and institutional investors capital-efficient exposure to the token through staking and yield strategies. The release said the increase "reflects the Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy and provides flexibility to buy back PURR shares as part of the Company's broader treasury management framework." The company said the timing, number and value of any shares repurchased will depend on the stock price, market conditions and legal requirements, and will remain at management's discretion. It said the board may extend, suspend or discontinue the program at any time without notice, and that there is no guarantee as to how many shares will ultimately be bought back. Beyond the dollar figures, the revised expiration date and the board's general statement of rationale, the release provides no additional detail on the buyback program.

item.title: Canadian retail sales rose 1.2% in August
item.description: Statistics Canada said sales reached $74.6 billion, with gains in all nine retail subsectors and a preliminary estimate pointing to a 0.7% rise in September.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada said retail sales in Canada rose 1.2% to $74.6 billion in August 2026, with increases recorded across all nine retail subsectors tracked in the survey. Motor vehicle and parts dealers posted the largest gain, also up 1.2%; gasoline stations rose 1.7%; and food and beverage retailers increased 1.1%, their first gain in three months, the agency said. Core retail sales, a measure that excludes gasoline stations and motor vehicle and parts dealers, rose 1.1% in August. In volume terms, which adjust the dollar figures for price changes, sales were also up 1.2%, indicating the increase reflected a rise in the quantity of goods sold rather than price alone. Provincial results varied. Ontario led with a 2.2% increase to $28.5 billion in retail sales, and British Columbia followed with a 2.1% increase to $10.0 billion. Sales declined in six provinces and territories — Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, New Brunswick, Alberta, Yukon and Nunavut — by between 0.1% and 0.6%, the agency said. E-commerce sales totalled $5.6 billion in August, up 1.1% from July and accounting for 7.6% of total retail trade for the month. Statistics Canada also published an advance estimate for September 2026, suggesting retail sales rose 0.7% for the month. The agency said the estimate is preliminary, based on a survey response rate of 58.5% compared with a historical average of 86.8%, and is subject to revision. The retail sales data are seasonally adjusted and reported in current dollars, the agency said.

item.title: Lighthouse Gold upsizes private placement to $6.45 million
item.description: Lighthouse Gold increased a private placement announced the day before, citing strong investor demand, with closing expected in early November.
item.content:encoded: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) announced on October 23, 2026 that it has increased the size of a private placement first announced October 22, 2026. The company attributed the increase to strong investor demand. The offering, originally up to 33,334,000 units at $0.18 per unit for gross proceeds of up to $6,000,120, has been increased to up to 35,835,600 units at the same $0.18 per unit, for gross proceeds of up to $6,450,408. Each unit comprises one common share and one-half of one share purchase warrant, so two units together carry one whole warrant. Each whole warrant entitles the holder to purchase one additional share at an exercise price of $0.28 for a period of two years from the closing date. The offering remains subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange, the release said, with closing expected on or about November 4, 2026. Securities issued under it will be subject to a four-month-and-one-day hold period from closing. The release did not name an agent, underwriter or finder for the offering, or disclose whether any insiders are participating. The company said it intends to use the proceeds for exploration and for general working capital purposes. Beyond that, the disclosure in this release is limited: it does not specify which exploration program or property the funds are earmarked for, or provide a budget breakdown between exploration and working capital.

item.title: Fewer young women meet activity guidelines, Statistics Canada reports
item.description: Statistics Canada's October Health Reports found that 46% of Canadian adults met weekly activity guidelines, with activity trends diverging by age and sex.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada published Health Reports for October 2026 on October 21, 2026, reporting that 46% of Canadian adults met the public health recommendation of at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week. The figures are drawn from accelerometer-measured data collected through the Canadian Health Measures Survey, which the agency said allows tracking of population-level activity trends over time, covering the period from 2007 to 2024. The agency said the share of men aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation held stable at 65% across that period, from 2007 to 2024. Over the same seventeen years, the share of women aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation declined, from 52% to 43%, according to the release. Statistics Canada did not state a reason for the divergence between the two groups. Adults aged 60 to 79 moved in the opposite direction from the youngest cohort of women: the agency reported a nine-percentage-point increase in the share meeting the recommendation for both men and women in that age group between 2007 and 2024. The release did not provide the specific starting and ending percentages for this age group, only the size of the increase. Statistics Canada said that knowing the share of adults who meet the 150-minute threshold does not tell the whole story, because it also matters how close those who fall short are to reaching it. The agency therefore also measured, for 2022 to 2024, the gap between non-compliant adults' actual activity levels and the recommended threshold. Over that 2022-to-2024 period, 34% of women aged 18 to 39 needed only 5 to 10 additional minutes of activity a day to meet the recommendation, the agency said. Among women aged 60 to 79, 50% were getting less than 10 qualifying minutes of activity a day over the same period. The release also reported that, from 2022 to 2024, approximately one-third of Canadian adults recorded at least 7,500 steps a day, with minimal differences between men and women on that measure over the period. The agency did not report a corresponding steps-based figure for 2007, so no comparable trend over time is available for step counts.

item.title: Pacific Imperial ends Brownell Lake option agreement
item.description: The company cited a lack of funding after its recent private placement was cancelled, as Eagle Plains Resources agreed to terminate the deal.
item.content:encoded: Pacific Imperial Mines Inc. (TSXV: PPM) announced on October 20, 2026 that it has reached a mutual agreement with Eagle Plains Resources Ltd. to terminate the Option Agreement on the Brownell Lake VMS project, effective immediately. The company said the termination resulted from "a lack of funding resulting from the recent cancellation of its private placement." The release does not identify which placement was cancelled, when, or on what terms, nor does it describe the terms of the original Option Agreement on the Brownell Lake project. Pacific Imperial said its board of directors is actively reviewing the company's strategic options and will be re-evaluating how to move forward. No timeline was given for that review. The release describes Pacific Imperial as a Vancouver-based mineral exploration company engaged in the acquisition, exploration, evaluation and development of mineral properties, with its current focus on the Babine and Fenton properties in British Columbia. The disclosure in this release is limited to the termination itself and gives no further operational or financial detail.

item.title: S&T Bancorp posts record quarterly earnings per share
item.description: The Pennsylvania bank holding company reported $38.6 million in third-quarter net income and continued its share buyback program.
item.content:encoded: S&T Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: STBA), the Indiana, Pennsylvania-based holding company for S&T Bank, reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $38.6 million, up from $36.6 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $35.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share was $1.09, which the company said represented a 6.9% increase from the prior quarter and a 19.8% increase from a year earlier, and which its own release headlined as a record. Profitability measures improved across the board: return on average assets was 1.55%, return on average equity was 10.84%, and return on average tangible shareholders' equity, a non-GAAP measure, was 14.81%. Net interest margin on a fully taxable equivalent basis expanded seven basis points from the prior quarter to 4.06%. Asset quality metrics moved favorably. Nonperforming assets decreased $3.7 million to $36.5 million, representing 0.45% of total loans plus other real estate owned. Net charge-offs totaled $2.1 million, or 0.10% of average loans. The allowance for credit losses was unchanged at $93.3 million, or 1.16% of total portfolio loans. On the balance sheet, total assets were flat at $9.9 billion. Total deposits decreased $22.2 million and total borrowings decreased $60.0 million to $215.3 million. Total portfolio loans decreased $4.4 million, which the company attributed to lower line utilization. S&T Bancorp said it has repurchased 3,169,294 shares, or 8.3% of shares outstanding, since the fourth quarter of 2025, at an average price of $42.09 per share. Approximately 35.3 million shares were outstanding at quarter-end. The company also declared a dividend of $0.37 per share. CEO Chris McComish said the results reflected "record earnings per share, record revenue and higher core profitability."

item.title: Norfolk Southern reports record quarterly revenue
item.description: The railroad posted $3.5 billion in third-quarter revenue and diluted earnings per share of $3.37, both up from a year earlier.
item.content:encoded: Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE: NSC) reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 22, 2026. Revenue was $3.5 billion, which the company's release described as a quarterly record, up $423 million, or 14%, from the third quarter of 2025. Income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, up $52 million, or 5%. Diluted earnings per share was $3.37, up $0.21, or 7%, from a year earlier. The operating ratio — the share of revenue consumed by operating expenses, where a lower figure indicates greater efficiency — was 67.4% for the quarter, compared with 64.6% in the third quarter of 2025. The company said volume increased 3% year over year. Norfolk Southern also reported adjusted results that it said exclude merger-related expenses and the effects of the Eastern Ohio incident. On that adjusted basis, income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, up 7% from a year earlier, with an adjusted operating ratio of 65.4%. Adjusted diluted earnings per share was $3.62, up 10% from the third quarter of 2025. CEO Mark George said: "Norfolk Southern delivered another quarter of solid execution, with record revenues, and strong earnings growth." The release described Norfolk Southern's network as spanning 22 states and moving approximately 7 million carloads annually, operating what it called the most extensive intermodal network in the eastern United States, and said rail transport helps its customers avoid approximately 15 million tons of carbon emissions each year.

item.title: Redwood AI special warrants trigger deadline penalty
item.description: Missing a 90-day filing deadline raises the units issuable under the company's $3.5 million special warrant financing by 10 percent.
item.content:encoded: Redwood AI Corp. (CSE: AIRX) (OTCQB: RDWCF) (Frankfurt: Y0N, WKN: A422EZ) said in an October 20, 2026 release that it did not meet the 90-day deadline to file a prospectus supplement qualifying the distribution of units issuable upon deemed exercise of the special warrants issued in its special warrant financing. The brokered private placement of 1,663,000 special warrants closed July 21, 2026 for aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $3.5 million, with Maxim Group LLC acting as exclusive placement agent. The 90-day deadline, which the release calls the Penalty Deadline, was set under the terms of the special warrants and an agency agreement between Redwood and Maxim dated July 16, 2026, entered into in connection with the offering. A special warrant of this kind converts into units of the company once a prospectus qualifying the underlying securities is filed, or on a backstop date if it is not; missing the filing deadline activates a penalty built into the warrant's own terms. That penalty increases the number of units issuable on deemed exercise of each special warrant from 1.00 to 1.10, for no additional consideration, the release said. Applied across the 1,663,000 special warrants outstanding, the total units issuable rises to 1,829,300 from 1,663,000, an increase of 166,300 units. Each unit comprises one common share of Redwood and one warrant exercisable at $2.48 per share for 60 months, according to the release. The units will be issued on the earlier of Redwood filing the prospectus supplement or November 22, 2026. The release does not state a revised date by which Redwood expects to file the prospectus supplement, nor does it give a reason the original deadline was missed. No further transaction step beyond the November 22, 2026 backstop date for deemed exercise is described in the release.

item.title: Noble Mineral closes Lucas Gold Project purchase
item.description: The TSX Venture-listed explorer closed its acquisition of the project from Canada Nickel Company and separately received exchange final acceptance for the transactions.
item.content:encoded: Noble Mineral Exploration Inc. (TSX-V: NOB) (FRANKFURT: NB7) (OTCQB: NLPXF) announced October 21, 2026 that it has closed the transactions under a Purchase Agreement with Canada Nickel Company Inc., under which Noble acquires the Lucas Gold Project. The transactions were previously announced in Noble's news releases dated July 13, 2026 and September 17, 2026. The company said Noble has received final acceptance from the TSX Venture Exchange for the transactions under the agreement. No further conditions or approvals are described in this announcement. For the main terms and conditions of the Purchase Agreement and a description of the Lucas Gold Project, the release directs readers to the news release Noble issued on September 17, 2026, rather than restating them here. This announcement discloses no purchase price, share or cash consideration, royalty, or other transaction term, and gives no description of the project's location, size, geology or exploration history. It states no use of proceeds and no next procedural step beyond the exchange acceptance already obtained. Noble describes itself, in the release's standard company description, as a Canadian-based junior exploration company that holds securities in Canada Nickel Company Inc., among other listed holdings. The release lists H. Vance White, President, as the contact for further information. Taken together, the two releases Noble points to — October 21 confirming closing and exchange acceptance, and September 17 setting out the terms — mean a reader following only today's announcement sees confirmation that a previously announced acquisition has completed, without the underlying deal terms restated in the same document.

item.title: M/I Homes reports lower third-quarter revenue, profit
item.description: The homebuilder's net income fell to $66.6 million on revenue of $1.076 billion as new contracts and deliveries each declined 2% from a year earlier.
item.content:encoded: M/I Homes, Inc. (NYSE: MHO), the Columbus, Ohio-based homebuilder marking its 50th anniversary in 2026, reported results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Third-quarter revenue was $1.076 billion, down 5% from $1.132 billion a year earlier. Net income was $66.6 million, or $2.56 per diluted share, against $106.5 million, or $3.92 per share, in the third quarter of 2025. Pre-tax income for the quarter was $86.9 million, down 38% from $139.8 million, a decline the company tied in part to $4.7 million of pre-tax inventory charges taken in the quarter, against $8.9 million for the first nine months. Gross margin was 20.9% as reported and 21.3% excluding the inventory charges. New contracts for the quarter fell 2% to 1,861 and homes delivered fell 2% to 2,241, at an average closing price of $460,000, with a cancellation rate of 12%. For the nine months, homes delivered fell 4% to 6,361 while new contracts rose 5% to 6,598, against 6,620 and 6,278, respectively, a year earlier. The company's backlog stood at 2,046 homes at September 30, 2026, down 7% from a year earlier, with a sales value of $1.103 billion, down 9%, and an average sales price of $539,000. M/I Homes operated 246 communities at quarter-end, up from 233 a year earlier. The company reported shareholders' equity of $3.3 billion and book value of $130 per share, both company records, along with $621 million of cash and equivalents, a homebuilding debt-to-capital ratio of 18%, a net debt-to-capital ratio of 2%, and zero borrowings outstanding on its $900 million credit facility. M/I Homes repurchased $50 million of its shares during the quarter. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, pre-tax income was $280.6 million, against $446.0 million a year earlier, and net income was $213.5 million, or $8.14 per diluted share, against $339.0 million, or $12.32 per share, in the first nine months of 2025. Chief executive Robert H. Schottenstein said the quarter's results 'reflect increasingly difficult market conditions, including higher mortgage interest rates, weaker demand and growing economic uncertainty,' adding that the company is 'well positioned to manage through this current cycle given the strength of our balance sheet, low debt levels, diverse product offerings and well-located communities.' The company said it will hold a conference call on October 21, 2026 at 10:30 a.m. ET to discuss the results. The release includes no forward guidance for the fourth quarter or full year beyond the comments attributed to Schottenstein.

item.title: China SXT ends additional share purchase right
item.description: The Nasdaq company and the purchasers in its October 8 offering agreed to terminate a right to buy up to $12 million more shares or warrants.
item.content:encoded: China SXT Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ: SXTC), based in Taizhou, China, announced October 21, 2026 that it has entered into a termination letter agreement with the purchasers in its registered direct offering announced October 8, 2026. The agreement, the company said, terminates the purchasers' additional purchase right contained in Section 2.4 of the securities purchase agreement that governed the offering. Under the original securities purchase agreement, that right had entitled the purchasers to buy up to $12 million of the company's Class A ordinary shares, pre-funded warrants, or a combination of the two, exercisable within a 30-day period following the offering's closing. A right of this kind gives investors in a financing a window to increase their position on terms already fixed in the initial agreement. With the termination letter agreement now in place, the company said the purchasers 'no longer have any right, claim or entitlement to make an additional purchase' under that section of the agreement. The release states that provision is the one affected by the termination. The company said all other provisions of the securities purchase agreement remain in full force and effect, and that the shares and any other securities already issued to purchasers under the October 8 offering are not affected by the termination. This announcement does not restate the gross proceeds, share count or pricing of the October 8 offering, nor does it state a reason the purchasers and the company agreed to terminate the additional purchase right. There is no stated use of proceeds or further procedural step in this release. It is limited to confirming the termination of the Section 2.4 right and that the securities purchase agreement's other provisions continue to apply.

item.title: Mijem Newcomm Tech launches up to $300,000 placement
item.description: The CSE-listed company's non-brokered offering carries three-year warrants that need shareholder approval before they can be issued.
item.content:encoded: Mijem Newcomm Tech Inc. (CSE: MJEM.X) said Oct. 19, 2026 that it will offer up to 6,000,000 units in a non-brokered private placement at $0.05 per unit, for gross proceeds of up to $300,000. Each unit comprises one common share and one common share purchase warrant. The warrants are exercisable at $0.05 per share for 36 months following the closing date. Taken together with the shares in each unit, the offering could result in the issuance of up to 12,000,000 common shares on a fully diluted basis if all warrants are exercised. The release did not state the company's current number of shares outstanding. The company said the offering is expected to close on or about November 30, 2026, and may close in one or more tranches, subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. Mijem said that because the offering could result in the issuance of more than 100% of its total outstanding securities, CSE Policy 4.6(2)(a) requires the company to obtain shareholder approval for the issuance of the warrants at its next shareholder meeting. If that approval is not obtained, the warrants will be cancelled. All securities issued under the offering will be subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day after issuance, in accordance with Canadian securities law, the company said. It said net proceeds from the offering will be used for working capital. The release did not describe Mijem's business, name any participating investors, or state whether any insiders are subscribing. It also gave no agent or finder, consistent with a non-brokered offering.

item.title: Canada's CPI rises 3.1% in September on energy prices
item.description: Statistics Canada said energy and gasoline prices drove the acceleration from August's 3.0% annual pace, even as food inflation eased to its slowest pace since mid-2024.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada said the Consumer Price Index rose 3.1% year over year in September 2026, up from a 3.0% increase in August. On a monthly basis the index rose 0.1% on an unadjusted basis, or 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis. The agency said energy prices led the September acceleration. It said crude oil prices increased during the month, reaching their highest level since May, "amid ongoing uncertainty about the wars in the Middle East." Gasoline prices rose 27.8% year over year in September, up from a 22.8% increase in August. Energy prices overall rose 19.0% year over year, compared with 15.4% in August. Excluding gasoline, the CPI rose 2.2% year over year in September, down from 2.4% in August. The agency said transportation costs, which include gasoline, rose 8.4% year over year in September. Prices for food purchased from stores rose 1.7% year over year, after increasing 2.8% in August, which it said was the smallest yearly increase in that category since May 2024. Shelter prices rose 1.8% year over year in September, up from 1.5% in August, which the agency attributed to higher fuel oil costs and increases in homeowners' insurance. Statistics Canada said five provinces experienced faster price growth in September, primarily due to elevated gasoline and fuel oil costs, and that Atlantic Canada showed notably higher inflation when energy costs were excluded from the regional comparison.

item.title: Gunnison Copper's ADRs set to trade on NYSE American
item.description: The Level II depositary receipt program begins trading October 26 under 'GUNN,' with no new shares issued and no capital raised through the listing.
item.content:encoded: Gunnison Copper Corp. (TSX: GCU, OTC: GCUMF, FSE: 3XS0) said its American Depositary Receipts are expected to commence trading on the NYSE American under the ticker symbol "GUNN" at the opening of trading on or about Monday, October 26, 2026. The listing is subject to the effectiveness of the company's registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and final exchange approvals, the company said. Each ADR will represent thirty common shares of Gunnison, under a Level II ADR program with The Bank of New York Mellon acting as depositary bank. A Level II program allows a foreign company's existing shares to trade on a U.S. national exchange through depositary receipts, without the company raising new capital in the process. Starting October 23, 2026, United States shareholders may convert their Gunnison common shares into ADRs through BNY. The company said explicitly that the ADR program does not constitute a new offering of securities, and that no additional common shares are being issued and no capital is being raised in connection with the NYSE American listing. Gunnison's shares will continue to trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange, the OTCQB market and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange alongside the new U.S. listing. The release described Gunnison as a multi-asset copper developer and producer controlling the Cochise Mining District in Arizona. The company's flagship Gunnison Copper Project carries a measured and indicated mineral resource in its main pit of more than 846 million tons at a copper grade of 0.33%, containing 5.19 billion pounds of copper, according to the release. A preliminary economic assessment completed in March 2026 for the project estimated an after-tax net present value, at an 8% discount rate, of $2 billion, an internal rate of return of 23% and a payback period of 3.9 years; full detail is in a technical report titled "Gunnison Project NI 43-101 Technical Report, Preliminary Economic Assessment, Cochise County, Arizona, USA," with an effective date of March 18, 2026, filed on SEDAR+. Gunnison's Johnson Camp Mine is currently producing finished copper cathode through an on-site SX/EW facility, which the company said is fully funded by Nuton LLC, a Rio Tinto venture, with capacity of up to 25 million pounds of finished copper cathode annually. The release said Gunnison is supplying copper from that operation to the U.S. defense sector and to Amazon Web Services.

item.title: WesCan brings third Provost well into production
item.description: The well was drilled, completed and tied in within budget following a $1.3 million convertible debenture financing, with water cut falling since start-up, the company said.
item.content:encoded: WesCan Energy Corp. (TSXV: WCE) said its third multilateral horizontal well in the Provost area of east-central Alberta, designated 105/15-21-38-3W4, began producing on October 9, 2026. The company said the well was drilled, completed, equipped and tied in within budget, following a $1.3 million convertible debenture financing. The release did not disclose the debenture's interest rate, conversion price or closing date. The company said the well remains in the early stage of its clean-up and flow-back period. Water cut, the share of water in the fluid produced, has fallen every day since start-up to approximately 58%, as load fluid used during completion is recovered, with oil rates rising as the water cut declines. WesCan said the well is being produced at a steady, controlled rate. This is the third multilateral well WesCan has brought onto production in the Provost area; a multilateral well drills more than one horizontal leg from a single surface location. Chief executive Leo Berezan said: 'Delivering a third Provost multilateral on budget tells us this program is repeatable. Water cut has come down every single day since start-up and oil rates are climbing with it.' Separately, WesCan said Sohaib Abbas has rejoined the company's board of directors, effective October 19, 2026; the release gave no further detail on the appointment. WesCan is headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, and describes itself in the release as focused on oil and gas exploration and production in the Provost area of east-central Alberta. Beyond the figures above, the release disclosed no additional production data, such as a flow rate in barrels per day, and gave no forecast for when water cut is expected to stabilize. Disclosure in this update is limited to what is stated here.

item.title: Loyalist discloses grade-tonnage data for Tully gold estimate
item.description: The data, drawn from the June 2026 technical report on the Timmins-area project, shows how resource tonnes and grade shift at different cut-off grades.
item.content:encoded: Loyalist Exploration Limited (CSE: PNGC) released additional grade-tonnage sensitivity data for the 2026 mineral resource estimate on its wholly owned Tully Gold Project in the Timmins Gold Camp of northeastern Ontario. The base-case estimate, using a 1.1 gram-per-tonne gold cut-off, reports indicated resources of 1.62 million tonnes grading 3.16 grams per tonne gold for 164,000 ounces, and inferred resources of 0.95 million tonnes grading 2.03 grams per tonne for 62,000 ounces. The sensitivity table applies a 1.25-metre minimum mining width, a constraint not used in the base-case estimate above, and shows how resource tonnes and grade shift at higher cut-off grades. At a 3.00 gram-per-tonne cut-off, Loyalist reported 407,000 indicated tonnes grading 9.19 grams per tonne for 120,000 ounces, and 150,000 inferred tonnes grading 6.45 grams per tonne for 31,000 ounces. At a 2.50 gram-per-tonne cut-off, the company reported 500,000 indicated tonnes grading 7.98 grams per tonne for 128,000 ounces and 205,000 inferred tonnes grading 5.43 grams per tonne for 36,000 ounces. At a 2.00 gram-per-tonne cut-off, indicated tonnes rose to 633,000 at 6.78 grams per tonne for 138,000 ounces, with inferred tonnes of 313,000 at 4.34 grams per tonne for 44,000 ounces. At a 1.50 gram-per-tonne cut-off, Loyalist reported 824,000 indicated tonnes grading 5.61 grams per tonne for 149,000 ounces and 436,000 inferred tonnes grading 3.60 grams per tonne for 51,000 ounces. At the 1.10 gram-per-tonne cut-off under this same mining-width constraint, the figures were 1,014,000 indicated tonnes at 4.80 grams per tonne for 156,000 ounces and 604,000 inferred tonnes at 2.96 grams per tonne for 57,000 ounces. President and chief executive Errol Farr said the sensitivity data "provides important additional insight" as the company advances a Preliminary Economic Assessment, and that it demonstrates "how the resource responds to higher cut-off grades," highlighting "the presence of a higher-grade core." The underlying technical report was prepared by qualified persons Curtis Ferron, Eugene Puritch and Charles Spath of P&E Mining Consultants Inc., with an effective date of June 15, 2026, and filed on SEDAR+ on August 21, 2026. Loyalist first announced the mineral resource estimate on July 7, 2026, and the filing of the technical report on August 21, 2026. The company said the newly released sensitivity data will factor into its approach to the Preliminary Economic Assessment, without specifying a timeline for that assessment.

item.title: VinFast posts 85.5% revenue growth for second quarter
item.description: EV deliveries rose 96% year over year to 70,085 units, while revenue reached US$1.2 billion on strength in Vietnam and expanding international markets.
item.content:encoded: VinFast Auto Ltd. (NASDAQ: VFS) reported unaudited financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Total revenue reached VND 30,340.9 billion, or US$1,203.7 million, up 32.9% from the first quarter of 2026 and 85.5% from the second quarter of 2025. The company delivered 70,085 electric vehicles in the quarter, an increase of 20% from the prior quarter and 96% from a year earlier, alongside 286,039 electric scooters and e-bikes, up 100% quarter over quarter and 311% year over year. Vehicle sales contributed VND 28,833.1 billion (US$1,143.9 million) of total revenue, up 33.4% quarter over quarter and 92.7% year over year. VinFast said international markets accounted for approximately 11% of total EV deliveries in the quarter, and that it operated 474 showrooms globally. In Vietnam, the company said it held approximately 38% market share, a position it said it has held for 22 consecutive months since September 2024. VinFast said it ranked first in the Philippines, fifth in India and eighth in Indonesia in the battery-electric vehicle category during the quarter. The company reported more than 12,700 reservations for its VF 8 model and more than 28,700 reservations for its VF 2 model within days of each vehicle's respective launch. The company said it has launched the VF Wild range-extended electric vehicle in Vietnam, with an international rollout planned for 2027. VinFast also said it is preparing a Level 4 autonomous robotaxi pilot using 200 vehicles in Can Gio, planned for late 2027, alongside its existing electric-vehicle and e-scooter lines. Pham Nhat Quan Anh, VinFast's chief executive and chairman, said the company "entered the second half of 2026 with strong momentum across our core markets and continued progress in expanding our global platform." Chief Financial Officer Lan Anh Nguyen said results "reflect continued strong revenue growth in our core electric mobility business as we scale vehicle volumes." VinFast said it continues to expand across Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines, India, the Middle East, North America and Europe, operating a combined 474 showrooms across those markets as of the quarter's end.

item.title: Loyalist ends private placement, closes shares-for-debt deal
item.description: The CSE-listed explorer said no further tranches of its placement will close, while it settled $113,285 of debt through a separate share issuance.
item.content:encoded: Loyalist Exploration Limited (CSE: PNGC) said it has terminated its previously announced non-brokered private placement, originally announced on August 10, 2026, and that no further tranches or closings will be completed. The company said the first tranche of that offering, consisting of 25,000,000 common shares at $0.04 each for gross proceeds of $1,000,000 and closed on August 31, 2026, represents the offering's final closing. Haywood Securities Inc. acted as finder, receiving $37,200 in cash and 930,000 warrants at $0.075 until August 2028. Separately, Loyalist closed a shares-for-debt transaction, settling an aggregate of $113,285 of outstanding indebtedness owed to certain creditors through the issuance of 2,832,125 common shares, also priced at $0.04 each. Of that total, $45,000 owed to president and chief executive Errol Farr and vice-president of exploration Leonard Mackenzie was settled through the issuance of 1,125,000 shares combined. All shares issued in the transaction carry a hold period of four months and one day. Loyalist said it is relying on exemptions from the formal valuation and minority approval requirements in sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 for the related-party portion of the debt settlement, on the basis that neither component of the transaction exceeded 25% of the company's market capitalization. Separately, it said proceeds of the placement's first tranche are funding ongoing National Instrument 43-101 technical work on its Tully project, including a resource estimate and a preliminary economic assessment, as well as continuing production permitting work.

item.title: Lexaria reports animal-study results for CBD formulation
item.description: The company says one new DehydraTECH-CBD formulation produced a 566% improvement in brain absorption in an animal study, and has filed three related patent applications.
item.content:encoded: Lexaria Bioscience Corp. (NASDAQ:LEXX), which describes itself as a global innovator in drug-delivery platforms, said on October 15, 2026 that it has results from an animal study designated GLP-1-A26-1. The study evaluated formulation enhancements using both DehydraTECH-CBD compositions and DehydraTECH-semaglutide glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) compositions, with the stated aims of exploring potential for additional improved performance and staking new intellectual property claims. The release's single headlined figure concerns one CBD formulation, designated ALT2: in brain tissue sampled eight hours after dosing, it produced a mean concentration of 62.8 ± 34.3 ng/g, compared with 9.42 ± 1.91 ng/g for the study's reference formulation. The company characterizes that difference as a 566% improvement in mean brain absorption of DehydraTECH-CBD. The study was conducted in Sprague-Dawley rats across eleven treatment arms, with pharmacokinetics measured in blood plasma and in brain tissue over a period the release describes as running from eight to twenty-four hours after dosing. Alongside the CBD arms, the study tested DehydraTECH-semaglutide formulations of the GLP-1 compound semaglutide, which the release describes as pursuing the same two goals: additional improved performance and new intellectual property claims. Lexaria said it has already filed three new patent applications related to the formulations evaluated in the study, to protect this new intellectual property. The release states plainly that because these patent applications are not yet published, the company will not be providing full details of all the specific formulations evaluated — a limit the company places on its own disclosure, stated in those terms in the release. Chief executive Rich Christopher was quoted in the release: 'We are delighted that certain new formulations in this Study achieved our highest-ever DehydraTECH pharmaceutical-grade relative absorption performance.' The quote is general to the study's formulations as a group, and the release does not tie it to any single figure or treatment arm among those described above, including the 566% brain-absorption result. The release was issued from Kelowna, British Columbia — Lexaria's home base — under an October 15, 2026 dateline, and distributed through TheNewswire. It closes with Lexaria's standard forward-looking-statement disclaimer, cautioning that factors including regulatory uncertainty and competitive pressure could cause actual results to differ from any expectations suggested by the study, a caution that applies to every figure reported above.

item.title: Robo.ai shareholders to vote on 1-for-25 reverse split
item.description: The Nasdaq-listed, Dubai-based company set an October 26 meeting on the share consolidation, record date October 14, effective date November 6 if approved.
item.content:encoded: Robo.ai Inc. (Nasdaq: AIIO), a UAE-based, U.S.-listed company, has called an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for October 26, 2026, to approve a 1-for-25 reverse stock split of all classes of its ordinary shares. The meeting is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET (4:30 p.m. Dubai time) at the Meydan Grandstand, sixth floor, in Dubai, with a record date of October 14, 2026. If shareholders approve it, the split will take effect November 6, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. ET, consolidating every 25 existing shares into one. The company's 13,817,501 Class A ordinary shares would become 552,701 Class A shares, and its 222,116,290 Class B ordinary shares would become 8,884,684 Class B shares. The post-split shares will trade under a new CUSIP, G6693P130, the company said. A reverse stock split reduces the number of shares outstanding by combining multiple shares into one, without changing a shareholder's proportional stake in the company other than for fractional adjustments. Robo.ai said no fractional shares will be issued under the proposed 1-for-25 split: a shareholder otherwise entitled to a fraction of a share will instead receive a full share. Robo.ai said it expects the Class B trading price to increase proportionately once the split takes effect, though it gave no assurance the post-split price would reach twenty-five times its level beforehand; the post-split shares will trade under a new CUSIP, G6693P130. The October 26 meeting will also consider increasing authorized share capital by up to 25 million new Class A ordinary shares and 280 million new Class B ordinary shares, and adopting a seventh amended and restated memorandum and articles of association. Robo.ai is headquartered in Dubai and lists its Class B ordinary shares on Nasdaq under the ticker AIIO. The release sets out the mechanics of the proposed split and the meeting but does not state a reason for the consolidation; completion depends on shareholder approval, and if approved, the company said the split becomes effective November 6, 2026.

item.title: NXG Cushing Midstream Energy Fund to rename, broaden mandate
item.description: The fund's Board of Trustees approved renaming it and broadening its investment policy from midstream energy to energy infrastructure, effective December 18.
item.content:encoded: The NXG Cushing® Midstream Energy Fund (NYSE: SRV), a closed-end fund, said its Board of Trustees has approved changing the fund's name to The NXG Cushing® Energy Infrastructure Fund, effective December 18, 2026. The fund's ticker symbol, SRV, and its CUSIP, 231631300, will remain unchanged, according to the announcement, which was released October 16, 2026, from the fund's Dallas offices. Alongside the name change, the Board approved amending the fund's non-fundamental investment policies. The fund's rule requiring at least 80% of its assets to be invested in a defined category will shift that category from "midstream energy investments" to "energy infrastructure investments." The release states that as of October 15, 2026, approximately 90% of the Fund's net assets, plus borrowings for investment purposes, already consisted of energy infrastructure investments, and that the Fund therefore does not anticipate any change to its investment approach or rebalancing of its portfolio as a result of the amendment. No shareholder approval or action is required for either the name change or the policy amendment, the release said. No shareholder vote or other approval was required for either change, the release said, and investors need take no action; the fund's New York Stock Exchange listing and CUSIP are unaffected. Beyond the name, the policy amendment and the asset figures above, the release discloses no further detail about the Board's reasoning.

item.title: Emergent Metals restates Q2 financials, updates Lahontan deal
item.description: The TSX Venture-listed explorer corrected prior filings and said shareholders will vote on its acquisition by Lahontan Gold on December 4.
item.content:encoded: Emergent Metals Corp. (TSXV: EMR, OTCQB: EGMCF, FRA: EML) has filed amended and restated unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, replacing the statements and management's discussion and analysis it originally filed on August 28, 2026. The company said the amended filings "correct certain accounting and disclosure matters identified following the filing of the Original Filings," without specifying what those matters were. The restatement reduced share capital and accumulated other comprehensive loss by US$231,040. It increased comprehensive loss by US$263,894 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and by US$297,428 for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Emergent said the corrections had no effect on the company's assets, liabilities, net loss, total equity or cash balance. Separately, Emergent provided an update on its proposed acquisition by Lahontan Gold Corp. under an arrangement agreement dated September 15, 2026. Under a plan of arrangement, a court-supervised process used in Canada to combine companies, Lahontan would acquire all of Emergent's issued and outstanding common shares in exchange for 0.3115 of a Lahontan share for each Emergent share held — equivalent to about one Lahontan share for every 3.21 Emergent shares. The TSX Venture Exchange has given conditional acceptance to the transaction. Emergent said its shareholders are scheduled to vote on the arrangement at a meeting set for December 4, 2026, and that completion remains subject to shareholder approval, court approval, final TSXV acceptance and other required approvals. The release pointed to further transaction details in Emergent's September 16, 2026 news release and to the arrangement agreement itself, filed on SEDAR+. The company also reminded holders of common share purchase warrants issued in private placements completed on November 14 and 19, 2024 that those warrants are scheduled to expire on November 14 and 19, 2026, respectively, at an exercise price of C$0.10. The release described the warrants as non-transferable and said no extension is currently intended. The release does not state a termination fee, identify a special committee, or say whether the transaction was negotiated at arm's length. It noted that the arrangement agreement and plan of arrangement are available under Emergent's and Lahontan's respective profiles on SEDAR+.

item.title: Azitra to execute 1-for-10 reverse stock split
item.description: The NYSE American-listed dermatology biopharmaceutical company's shares begin trading on a split-adjusted basis October 26, 2026.
item.content:encoded: Azitra, Inc. (NYSE American: AZTR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for precision dermatology, said its board of directors has approved a 1-for-10 reverse stock split of its common stock. The split takes effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern time on October 26, 2026, and the company's shares will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis under a new CUSIP number, 05479L401, when the market opens that day. A reverse stock split combines multiple existing shares into a single new share, reducing the number outstanding without changing a holder's proportional ownership, apart from the effect of any fractional-share cash-out. Azitra's stockholders authorized the board, at the company's June 15, 2026 annual meeting, to select a ratio between 1-for-2 and 1-for-30; the board approved the final ratio of 1-for-10, together with the October 26 effective date, on October 14, 2026. The change will reduce outstanding shares from 60,603,742 to approximately 6,060,374. Azitra said stockholders holding shares through a brokerage account will have their holdings automatically adjusted to reflect the new ratio. Those entitled to a fractional share will instead receive cash, without interest, calculated from the average closing price of Azitra's common stock over the five trading days immediately preceding the effective date. The stock will continue to trade on NYSE American under the symbol AZTR, now under a new CUSIP, 05479L401, with Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Co. as transfer agent. Azitra describes itself as a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for precision dermatology. Its disclosed pipeline includes ATR-COSF, a recombinant protein candidate, and ATR-04, an investigational live biotherapeutic for EGFR inhibitor-associated rash, which the company said has received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The release describes only the mechanics of the reverse split — the ratio, the effective date, the resulting share count and the fractional-share treatment. It does not state a business rationale for the chosen ratio or the timing of the change.

item.title: Canadian wholesale sales fell 1.6% in August
item.description: Statistics Canada said sales excluding petroleum and grain products dropped to $91.6 billion, even as sales ran 7.2% above a year earlier.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada reported that wholesale sales, excluding petroleum, petroleum products, other hydrocarbons, and oilseed and grain, fell 1.6% to $91.6 billion in August 2026. The agency said sales decreased in five of the sector's seven subsectors, together accounting for 70.6% of total wholesale sales. The largest decline came from the motor vehicle and motor vehicle parts and accessories subsector, which fell 3.8% to $15.1 billion. The agricultural supplies industry group posted the next-largest decrease, down 12.4% to $3.5 billion. The overall decline was moderated by the building material and supplies subsector, which rose 1.4% to $14.1 billion. Statistics Canada said wholesale sales were 7.2% higher in August than in the same month a year earlier. In volume terms — which adjust for price changes — wholesale sales, under the same exclusions, fell 1.8% in August. Wholesale inventories, excluding the same petroleum and grain-related categories, were unchanged in August at $141.0 billion. The inventory-to-sales ratio rose from 1.51 in July to 1.54 in August, a measure of how many months it would take to clear existing inventory at the current sales pace. Ontario posted the largest provincial decline, down 1.6% to $47.8 billion, following six months of consecutive increases, and Saskatchewan posted the second-largest decrease, down 8.2% to $3.8 billion. Statistics Canada also reported gains in several smaller jurisdictions: Prince Edward Island rose 5.1% to $125.1 million, Nova Scotia rose 0.6% to $1,400.1 million, and Alberta rose 0.7% to $10,378.9 million, while Nunavut rose 43.4% to $13.9 million. Statistics Canada said this release's content was produced with the assistance of a generative artificial intelligence tool and refined and verified by the agency's own experts.

item.title: Goldgroup completes C$101 million strategic investment in Luca Mining
item.description: Goldgroup Mining acquired subscription receipts expected to convert into roughly 19.9% of Luca Mining once its Cozamin Mine acquisition closes.
item.content:encoded: Goldgroup Mining Inc. (TSXV: GORO) (NYSE American: GORO) said it completed a C$101,123,662 strategic investment in Luca Mining Corp. on October 14, 2026, acquiring 101,123,662 subscription receipts at a price of C$1.00 per receipt. The receipts were issued as part of a bought-deal private placement that Luca is conducting in connection with its proposed acquisition of the Cozamin Mine, which the release refers to as the "Cozamin Acquisition" without further describing its terms. A subscription receipt is a security that converts into a common share once specified conditions are met, rather than granting share ownership immediately. Here, the receipts convert into Luca common shares once release conditions are satisfied, which the release says include completion of the Cozamin Acquisition. Goldgroup said it may elect to convert its receipts early, provided doing so would not take its holding above 19.9% of Luca's outstanding shares without further approval. Following conversion, Goldgroup said it will hold 101,123,662 Luca common shares, representing approximately 19.9% of Luca's outstanding shares on a non-diluted basis. The release does not state Luca's total share count on a diluted basis, nor does it give the total size of the bought-deal offering of which Goldgroup's receipts were a part. Goldgroup also secured an investor rights agreement with Luca. While Goldgroup holds at least 10% of Luca's shares, the agreement gives it the right to participate in future equity financings and top up its holding in relation to dilutive issuances, and the right to nominate two persons to Luca's board of directors. The release states that Goldgroup "intends to assess opportunities relating to its investment in Luca" and that, depending on its strategic priorities, market conditions and its evaluation of Luca's business, it may acquire additional securities, exercise its board nomination rights, or dispose of some or all of its position. The release does not name Luca's stock ticker or exchange, does not name any underwriter or agent for Luca's offering, and does not describe the terms of the Cozamin Mine acquisition — the price, the seller, or Luca's other obligations — beyond referring to it as a pending acquisition that conversion of the receipts is conditioned on. Goldgroup's contacts for the release are listed as Javier Reyes, chief executive officer, and Sophia Shane, in corporate development.

item.title: US consumer prices rose 0.6% in September
item.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% over the year.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers rose 0.6 percent in September 2026 on a seasonally adjusted basis. Over the 12 months ending in September, the index rose 3.7 percent on a not-seasonally-adjusted basis, the bureau said. The index for all items less food and energy — commonly referred to as core CPI — rose 0.3 percent in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, and was up 2.6 percent over the year, not seasonally adjusted, according to the release. The bureau attributed much of the monthly increase to energy prices, stating that "the index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase." Over the 12-month period, it said "the energy index increased 20.4 percent... due in large part to the index for gasoline rising 34.2 percent." Shelter costs continued to rise: the bureau said "the shelter index rose 0.4 percent in September after rising 0.3 percent in August," with the shelter index up 3.2 percent over the year. The food index was unchanged in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, the bureau said, though it rose 2.5 percent over the preceding 12 months. The release reports the measured price changes for the month and the year; it includes no assessment of future price trends or monetary policy.

item.title: HawkEye 360 secures $36 million in new international contracts
item.description: The Q3 awards span more than 10 allied and partner nations across the Indo-Pacific, Middle East, Europe and the Americas, the company said.
item.content:encoded: HawkEye 360, Inc. (NYSE: HAWK) announced on October 15, 2026 that it secured $36 million in new international contracts during the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The release describes HawkEye 360 as "the global leader in signals intelligence data and analytics" and says the new awards reflect demand for its capabilities across more than 10 allied and partner nations. The release structures the new business as multi-year awards rather than one-time contracts, though it does not state the length of the multi-year terms or break the $36 million figure down by region, country or individual award. It groups the customers by region: the Indo-Pacific, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas. HawkEye 360 said these defense and intelligence customers are turning to its data and analytics "to strengthen situational awareness, identify emerging threats, and support timely operational decision-making" as they face what the company describes as increasingly complex security environments.
